future_check: If canonical authorities change, re-count blue components and sizes before tightening self_check.
rationale: The prior generator encoded a one-connected-blob grammar, but canonical rows include disconnected blue source cells and blue size 9. Rejecting those rows was a generator grammar error, not a data anomaly.
summary: The source blue set is not required to be one connected component.

future_check: Re-run the minimal-demo audit if profiles, rival set, or EXAMPLES_NEEDED change.
rationale: The five profiles isolate ordinary connected reflection, disconnected global reflection, column-priority/first-anchor behavior, inert decoys, and clipping/overlap. Fewer than five demonstrations leave canonical-fitting rivals alive in the tested schedule.
summary: Use a deterministic five-profile lesson schedule to make the subtle rule distinctions teachable.

future_check: Run check_generator_override_contract.py after any AXES or difficulty-policy change.
rationale: The prior generator silently ignored or failed to observe accepted overrides and accepted unknown keys. The repair makes grid_h, grid_w, n_dots, and blue_size exact-or-loud while keeping ordinary difficulty defaults independent.
summary: Declared override axes are exact domains and accepted values are never narrowed by difficulty.

future_check: Only normalize raw_code if repository policy explicitly reclassifies it from archival provenance to selected authority.
rationale: The selected executable authorities were text-divergent but behaviorally equivalent. Exact selected-source synchronization removes ambiguity without erasing archival provenance; execution parity confirms the archival spellings still agree on canonical pairs.
summary: Synchronize selected task-local target_code to canonical program_solution while preserving archival raw_code.

future_check: Keep oracle validity and lesson-quality validity separate in future grammar changes; a self_check rejection must not be described as an oracle crash.
rationale: A recombined scene with an unaligned sole dot is a valid oracle input and returns identity, but it is unsuitable teaching data because no active transformation is observable. self_check therefore enforces teaching usefulness rather than the full mathematical domain.
summary: self_check intentionally rejects semantically inert lessons even though the Racket oracle can execute them.
